# xtremax

> Extreme value modelling for JAX and NumPyro. NumPyro-native EVT distributions (GEV, GPD, Gumbel, Fréchet, Weibull) whose maths lives in pure JAX primitives that stay accurate and differentiable through the Gumbel limit ξ → 0 and in the far tail; stable quantiles, return levels and non-stationary return levels; temporal, spatial and spatiotemporal point processes (Poisson, renewal, Hawkes, marked, thinned) as pure functions, equinox operators and NumPyro likelihoods; and xarray-native block maxima, thresholds, declustering and extremal-index estimates. Use these instead of hand-writing EVT densities, return-level formulas, Poisson likelihoods or extraction loops.

One package, `xtremax`, installed from GitHub: `uv add "xtremax @ git+https://github.com/jejjohnson/xtremax.git"`; extra `[threshold]` (scikit-learn, for the quantile-regression threshold). Inference (MCMC, SVI, `Predictive`) is NumPyro's; GP priors on spatially varying parameters come from a GP library. Before writing a helper, search the capability index — every public name with a one-line summary. Code you add should keep three rules:

- **Distributions are NumPyro sites:** `numpyro.sample("obs", xtremax.GeneralizedExtremeValueDistribution(loc, scale, concentration), obs=y)`; start NUTS with `init_strategy=init_to_median`, since the default init can strand a GEV fit at ξ < -1, where the likelihood is unbounded.
- **Stable forms:** return levels from `xtremax.primitives.gev_return_level` / `gpd_return_level` (or `d.return_level(T)` on a GEV or GPD), tails from `*_survival`, never `icdf(1 - 1/T)` or `1 - cdf`; scipy's `genextreme` takes `c = -ξ`.
- **Padded events, explicit keys:** point-process events are a fixed-size `times` buffer plus a mask whose `True` entries come first; every sampler takes a PRNG key and a static buffer size (`max_events`, or `max_candidates` for thinning samplers).

Claude Code users can install the `xtremax` plugin: `/plugin marketplace add jejjohnson/xtremax`, then `/plugin install xtremax@xtremax`.

## Start here

- [Home](https://jejjohnson.github.io/xtremax/): what xtremax is, installation, a quickstart
- [Capability index](https://jejjohnson.github.io/xtremax/reference/capabilities/): every public name, grouped by module, with a summary
- [Building with agents](https://jejjohnson.github.io/xtremax/agents/): the Claude Code plugin, this file, and rules to paste into your project's AGENTS.md
- [Interop](https://jejjohnson.github.io/xtremax/interop/): how xtremax composes with NumPyro and pipekit without depending on pipekit
- [EVT distributions overview](https://jejjohnson.github.io/xtremax/evt-distributions-overview/): the five families side by side

## API reference

- [Overview](https://jejjohnson.github.io/xtremax/reference/)
- [Distributions](https://jejjohnson.github.io/xtremax/reference/distributions/): NumPyro GEV, GPD, Gumbel, Fréchet, Weibull with return levels, survival and moments
- [Primitives](https://jejjohnson.github.io/xtremax/reference/primitives/): pure JAX densities, CDFs, quantiles, return levels; non-stationary and spatial helpers
- [Extraction](https://jejjohnson.github.io/xtremax/reference/extraction/): block maxima, thresholds, declustering, extremal index on xarray
- [Point processes — overview](https://jejjohnson.github.io/xtremax/reference/point-processes/): domains, event histories, sample results, quadrature
- [Point processes — primitives](https://jejjohnson.github.io/xtremax/reference/point-process-primitives/): intensities, compensators, log-likelihoods, samplers, diagnostics
- [Point processes — operators](https://jejjohnson.github.io/xtremax/reference/point-process-operators/): equinox process objects with goodness of fit
- [Point processes — distributions](https://jejjohnson.github.io/xtremax/reference/point-process-distributions/): NumPyro wrappers for MCMC / SVI
- [Simulations](https://jejjohnson.github.io/xtremax/reference/simulations/): synthetic temperature, precipitation and wind extremes, GMST trajectories
